rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance – source of income protected in tenant selection
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may not discriminate in renting, including based on source of income (including Section 8 and public benefits). They may use any reasonable selection standard, such as ability to pay rent, as long as it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Housing Ordinance prohibits discrimination in real estate transactions such as:

exemption_conditions.condition: 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there are exempt

coverage.notes: Exemption applies only to owner-occupied 2-family dwellings.

rules.coverage_text: Real estate transactions in Cambridge, including viewing or renting an apartment and terms and conditions of tenancy. Protected categories include source of income (including Section 8 and public benefits).
rules.exemptions: Exemption for 2-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.interaction: If Probable Cause is found, either party may remove the case to Massachusetts Superior Court or to the Attorney General's Office.

tool_input.notes: This is the Cambridge Human Rights Commission page, mostly about general anti-discrimination rules. I recorded only the Fair Housing Ordinance rule because it lists source of income (Section 8, public benefits) as a protected category in renting, which limits tenant screening. The page has no rules on rent caps, evictions, deposits, application fees or algorithms. It gives no effective dates.
